newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH CENTRE PARTY MOVES FOR CONFIDENCE VOTE.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH CENTRE PARTY MOVES FOR CONFIDENCE VOTE.

text.p: Finland's opposition Centre Party said on Friday it would submit an interpellation against the left-right-green government's social and regional policy, forcing the cabinet to face a vote of confidence in parliament.
Centrist parliamentary group leader Aapo Saari told reporters that government party MPs, too, had been dissatisfied with a recent government report on social and regional policy.
The interpellation is the Centre Party's second against the five-party coalition since it took office two years ago.
The vote of confidence will be the sixth for Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen's cabinet.

Saari said the interpellation would be submitted today. The likely date for the government to deliver its formal response to the interpellation -- followed by plenary debate and the vote of confidence -- would be sometime in week 20 (May 12 to 18), he said.
The parliamentary groups of the five government parties control 141 seats in the 200-member single-chamber legislature where the Speaker does not vote.
